terms.grammar: adjective (participle of occupō); with in + ablative
evidence: Cic. Sen. 32: nēmō … cui fuerim occupātus
Cic. Off. 1.57: in patriā dēlendā occupātī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Busy with something is in aliquā rē occupātus. The opposite is ōtiōsus, at leisure (Cic. Tusc. 1.5); for “free, not busy” see available.

evidence: Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8.10.3: haec causa prīmōs mēnsēs occupābit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a task that takes up time or attention; its first sense is to seize (see occupy-seize).

evidence: Cic. Inv. 2.132: in aliēnīs negōtiīs dētinērī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly to hold back or detain; then to keep someone occupied.
Busy with affairs and work; also of a thing that gives much work (prōvincia negōtiōsa, Cic. Mur. 18).

phrases.latin: itaque nēmō adhūc convenīre mē voluit, cui fuerim occupātus
phrases.english: and so far no one has wanted to see me and found me busy

phrases.latin: Nihil mē interpellāstī, nōn enim occupātus eram.
phrases.english: You didn’t interrupt me at all: I wasn’t busy.

sources: Lewis & Short: occupo · Lewis & Short: detineo · Lewis & Short: negotiosus
